chapter_title: Concerning the Fifty Lord's Days; to what Mysterie
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶2:** Know that within [eac]h of the five external truths that the [GAP-1: primordial celestial] mind called forth from the Divine, there reside five spiritual faculties. These five are to be reckoned together with [GAP-2: one an]other, these five, and five times [GAP-3: multiplied yield the fullness of] their number. Yet at the time when [GAP-4: the divine influx descended into the lower mind,] the Divine Calling went down into the natural degree. The Reciprocal Will desired to ascend with it. And the Divine Calling together with the Receptive Submission [GAP-5: together constitute] twenty-five spiritual faculties distributed through their twenty-five particular functions — [GAP-6: which] are the derivative truths born from the celestial mind. The Divine Calling and [the Receptive Sub]mission were elevated into interior states by means of these faculties.

**¶3:** Just as their ori[gin,] the living celestial mind, raised itself into interior states through these faculties — by the same means all things in the interior and exterior degrees have been set in order. Indeed, these are what is signified by the fullness called pentecost: the fifty great states that are the [GAP-7: archetypes of the] consecrated states of spiritual life. They abstained from their own [nour]ishment — that which is merely self-derived.

**¶4:** So, from that state onward until [GAP-8: the state] of [the mani]festation of Divine Wisdom in its Splendour — the glorious influx that came [GAP-9: and restored] their nourishment, which is the [GAP-10: interior sustenance] of the spirit, which is the Divine Calling and the Receptive Submission — [GAP-11: that is to say,] that spiritual sustenance of good and truth. They rele[GAP-12: ased themselves into] all these fifty states of fullness, which [GAP-13: signify that] this living nourishment from the Divine suffices for all faculties. It filled them all with spiritual potency and abundance of goods and truths and life from the Divine. Wisdom [GAP-14: flows through] this living nourishment, so that [GAP-15: every faculty] became rich with interior good.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Happen you know that [in eac]h one of these five garments that the [First] Man summoned there are five powers. They shall be counted to the [number of each] other, these five, and five times [five is] their number. However, at the time [when] the Summons went down. The Answer wished to ascend with it. And the Summons with the Obedience [constitute] twenty-five characteristics in their twenty-five limbs, [which] are the sons of the Man. The Summons and [the Obed]ience were raised to the heights through them.

Just as their fa[ther] the living Man raised himself up through them, by these these other ones have set up all things a[bov]e and below. Indeed, these are what are called pentecost, the fifty great days that are the [archetypes of the] holy [d]ays. They fasted from their [foo]d, [w]hich is their own.

So, from that time until [the time] of [the adv]ent of Jesus the Splendour, the glorious one who came [ ... / ... t]heir food which is the [light] of sou[l], which is the Summons and the Obedience [that is] that spiritual food. They rele[ased themselves in] all these fifty days, which [signify that] this living food suffices for all of them. It filled them all with power and richness and life. Light [came through] this living food that [they all] became rich.

fills.explanation: The "First Man" is the standard Manichaean designation for the primordial celestial being who descends with the five garments/sons; this is the universal term in the Kephalaia.
The five powers are to be reckoned against each other's number (5 × 5 = 25), fitting the multiplicative logic that immediately follows with "five times five is their number."
The arithmetic of the passage requires "five times five is their number" to yield the twenty-five characteristics mentioned in the next sentence.
A temporal conjunction is needed to connect "at the time" with "the Summons went down," and "when" is the natural connector in Kephalaia prose for introducing the narrative of descent.
The Summons and Obedience together form/constitute the twenty-five characteristics; the editor's word correctly captures the structural conjunction of Call and Answer into a unified set of faculties.
The relative pronoun "which" correctly introduces the appositive clause identifying the twenty-five limbs as the sons of the Man.

The fifty great days are the primordial patterns (archetypes) of the holy days observed in worship; this fits the correspondential logic where celestial events are the prototypes of ritual observance.
The temporal frame "from that time until the time of the advent" is standard Kephalaia narrative structure for marking cosmological epochs.

In Manichaean cosmology the food/nourishment of the divine beings is the purified light; "the light of soul" denotes the interior luminous substance that is the Summons and Obedience, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "interior sustenance."
The phrase "that is" serves as an explicative connector identifying the Summons and Obedience with "that spiritual food," matching the spiritual reading's "that is to say."

Following the restoration of their food by Jesus the Splendour, the divine powers "released themselves in" the fifty days, meaning they were liberated into the fullness of the fifty archetypal states.

The fifty days are archetypes (as stated in ¶3), so "which signify that this living food suffices" fits the correspondential teaching that the days represent the sufficiency of divine nourishment for all faculties.

Light (Divine Wisdom) flowed through the living food as the vehicle of influx, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "flows through" — expressed in the Kephalaia's narrative register as "came through."

The result clause requires a subject: "that they all became rich" completes the sense that every faculty/power was enriched by the living food, matching the spiritual reading's "every faculty became rich."
